items.stem: A team wants to release a new version and validate it on production infrastructure before users hit it, with instant rollback. What should they use?

options.text: A staging deployment slot with a slot swap (and swap with preview)
options.rationale: Correct: slot swap gives warmed, zero-downtime releases with instant rollback.

options.text: Deleting and recreating the app each release
options.rationale: That causes downtime and data loss risk.

options.text: Editing files on the production app in place
options.rationale: In-place edits are not safely reversible.
Tier changes do not provide release validation.

items.explanation: Correct: slot swap gives warmed, zero-downtime releases with instant rollback.

items.stem: Which TWO let an App Service app read a database password without storing the secret in configuration or code? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A system-assigned managed identity for the app
options.rationale: Correct: managed identity removes stored credentials.

options.text: A Key Vault reference in app settings resolved by that identity
options.rationale: Correct: the app resolves the secret at runtime via the vault.

options.text: Committing the password to the Git repo
options.rationale: Secrets must not be in source control.

options.text: Putting the password in the container image

items.explanation: Correct: managed identity removes stored credentials.

items.stem: An app is CPU-bound under concurrent load but each request is light. What is the better first response?

options.rationale: Correct: more instances spread concurrent requests.

options.text: Scale up to a bigger single instance only
options.rationale: Scaling up alone may not help concurrency as well as scaling out.

items.explanation: Correct: more instances spread concurrent requests.
